text:
Two goalies with something to prove meet in Buffalo. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen had the net to himself at the Sabres' optional skate, and he comes in with his 100th career win from Saturday's 6-2 rout in Tampa and a season that has been more uneven than that night: .878 in 14 games, slightly below expected (-0.5). Last season he was +9.1. For the Rangers it's Joonas Korpisalo, a .940 save rate in three games and only his fourth start. With Igor Shesterkin lost for the season in October, the Rangers have had to live without a safety net, and they've done it by defending: 53% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances each side gets).

The injuries are what's testing them now. Pavel Dorofeyev is on injured reserve (he practiced in a red noncontact jersey) and Oliver Bjorkstrand is out until late January. Will Cuylle has moved up to the top line and Tye Kartye keeps earning minutes. J.T. Miller has a four-game point streak and is one assist from 500 for his career. Our numbers like Alexis Lafrenière most to score, at 29%.

Buffalo's top line is where the noise is. Tage Thompson has goals in four straight games, five in all, Zach Benson has six points in four, and Jiri Kulich has found his game between them. Benson is our sleeper for a point at 61%, above his season pace, because his line creates 3.97 expected goals per 60. Jack Quinn has goals in three straight. Our numbers flag all three wingers as due to cool, and the Sabres have taken only 46% of the expected goals over their last five.

Buffalo also takes 4.1 penalties a game, which is a lot of rope to give a team whose penalty kill allows 0.55 expected goals a night. The race says the stakes sit with the Sabres: 24% to make the playoffs, the Rangers 68%. Sam Carrick faces his old team for the first time, and Ryan McLeod plays his 400th game.
headline: Luukkonen back in, Korpisalo gets his turn
